401: Remember that billion bits per second? Here's the strange part. Your conscious mind works with about ten.
402: A fire hose, feeding a drinking straw.
403: So let's remove the straw. Senses dial, all the way up.
404: Congratulations. You now notice every sound in this café. Every flicker of light. Every thread of your socks.
405: Unfortunately, you notice them all at the same time.
406: It wouldn't feel like a superpower. It would feel like living inside a fire alarm.
407: Because your brain's real talent isn't collecting information. It's throwing most of it away.
408: Here's proof. In a famous experiment, people watched a short video of players passing a basketball, and counted the passes.
409: Halfway through, a person in a gorilla suit walked right through the scene. Roughly half of the viewers never saw it.
410: That's not a bug. That's your filter, doing its job.
411: And the filter is clever. In a classic study from the nineteen fifties, people heard two messages at once, one in each ear, and were told to ignore one of them.
412: They remembered almost nothing from the ignored ear. But about a third of them still noticed when it said their own name.
413: Quick side note: that's the cocktail party effect. It's why your name cuts through a noisy room.
414: So what would a real upgrade look like? Not more input. Better use of it.
415: Some blind people learn to see with sound. They click their tongue, and listen to the echoes, a bit like a bat.
416: Brain scans show those echoes being processed in an area that normally handles vision.
417: Their brains didn't get new senses. They found a new job for the old ones.
418: Verdict: the senses dial is already set close to perfect. So let's leave it, and try the next one. Memory.
